newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's T-Corp sees steady samurai demand.
newsitem.headline: Australia's T-Corp sees steady samurai demand.

text.p: Australia's New South Wales Treasury Corp (T-Corp) said on Wednesday it expected continued strong demand from Japanese investors for its samurai bond issues, which would again make up the bulk of its overseas debt issuance in 1997/98 (July-June).

"It's still our preference to tap the Japanese for the bulk of our offshore issuance because it's so attractive," T-Corp's General Manager of Treasury Stephen Knight told reporters after a breakfast function.

Earlier T-Corp, the borrowing arm of the New South Wales state government, announced it would borrow A$4.9 billion in 1997/98, with 40 to 50 percent percent of that debt issuance carried out offshore.
This issuance was up from A$3.9 billion in 1996/97, largely because of larger maturing borrowings and a lower bottom line surplus from the government.
"We anticipate that there will be steady demand from Japan," Knight said.
Some commentators had predicted that Japanese demand for such samurai bonds would shift to the United States as the U.S. dollar continued to appreciate and U.S. interest rates rose, he said.
"I think those calls are grossly exaggerated," he said.
Knight said Japanese demand for Australian dollar denominated samurais was likely to remain strong, even if there is a slowdown or reversal in the Australian dollar's appreciation against the Yen.
"I don' think the Japanese are expecting the same sort of appreciation of the A$ that they've seen in the past," he said.
"The interest rate differential is the more important thing now. You've still got some interest rate differential even if the currency stabilises."
Knight said that even if there was a move into U.S. dollar denominated samurai bonds, T-Corp also had the flexibility to issue U.S. dollar samurais.
